🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE OPPOSITION'S SCRIPT: SUBORDINATION SOLD AS MODERNITY</u>

In Contralínea, philosopher Fernando Buen Abad Domínguez breaks down how Mexico's right-wing alliance works long before any pact is signed: "The plunder begins in the dictionary long before it settles into the institutions." The cognitive war doesn't need to abolish the Constitution — it's enough to make it invisible, repainting dependence as opportunity and sovereignty as backwardness. Mexico's opposition, he argues, doesn't arrive wrapped in foreign flags; it shows up speaking the national language, selling the handover of strategic assets as the price of the future.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>WASHINGTON FREEZES MEXICAN AVOCADO EXPORTS — MEXICO ANSWERS</u>

The US suspended USDA inspections in Michoacán over a vague "security threat" to its personnel, halting shipments from the state that supplies 80% of the avocados Americans eat. Packers were told only fruit received before August 4 can still be processed. Mexico didn't wait: Sheinbaum's government requested an urgent meeting with the USDA, offered Senasica inspectors as replacements, and deployed 1,500 soldiers to the avocado belt. Mexico sells, Washington blocks — and Mexico still fixes it.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>AYOTZINAPA CASE: EX-GOVERNOR AGUIRRE ARRESTED FOR COVER-UP</u>

Mexico's FGR detained Ángel Aguirre Rivero, governor of Guerrero when the 43 normalistas were disappeared in 2014, for allegedly hiding evidence of the students' whereabouts. Under the case's "new investigation model," prosecutors reanalyzed the file and accredited his probable participation — the arrest warrant was executed today. Sheinbaum had announced last week that news was coming on the 43. The impunity that defined the old regime is being dismantled file by file.

‍JACOBIN: Mexican Sovereignty in the Era of the Donroe Doctrine August 4, 2026 | 🟢 📰 A US outlet finally says it: four CIA agents ran counter-narcotics raids inside Mexico wearing Chihuahua state police uniforms — their third op since January, part of a "secret war on cartels." 🔍 The rare piece in US media that treats Mexican sovereignty as the starting point, not the obstacle. • "a playbook not much different than counterterrorism missions" • "clandestinely and illegally inside Mexico"
banner: CIA Ran Secret Raids Inside Mexico

text: ‍FOX NEWS: US pauses government operations in cartel-ridden Mexican state August 6, 2026 | 🔴 📰 Fox stamps "cartel-ridden" on Michoacán after the US halted avocado inspections over a threat. NBC ran the same story straight: "suspends avocado inspections due to threat." 🤡 Fox buries the economy at the bottom: Mexico sold $3.65B in avocados to the US in 2025, and exports are up 35% this year. The state security secretary said he knew of no direct incident involving inspectors. • "a risk of violence from terrorist groups, cartels, gangs and criminal organizations" • "unaware of any direct incidents involving the avocado inspectors"

‍AP: US targets reported leader of powerful Mexican drug cartel with $25M reward August 5, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Washington puts $100M in bounties on CJNG figures — $25M on "El Pelón," El Mencho's stepson and a dual US citizen — plus visa bans for family members and business associates. 🔍 The frame leads with US pressure; buried lower: it was the Mexican military that killed El Mencho in February, with the US in a supporting intelligence role. • "aimed at crippling the organization's leadership" • "This is a fight against CJNG that we are just beginning" — DEA's Terrance Cole
banner: US Puts $100M in Bounties on CJNG

text: ‍BLOOMBERG: Sheinbaum's Approval Jumps as Mexico Inflation Cools to Five-Year Low August 6, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Bloomberg's own AtlasIntel poll: Sheinbaum jumps 8 points to 57% as inflation hits 3.1% — and 43% now expect a stronger job market. 🇲🇽 Straight report, no editorializing — a month after the same pollster's sub-50% reading got the doom framing. Two-thirds of Mexicans back criminal complaints over the 17 Mexican deaths in ICE custody or operations. • "lowest annual inflation reading since the end of 2020" • "about 61% of respondents hold a negative view of ICE"

🇲🇽📊 <u>ANALYSTS CUT MEXICO INFLATION FORECAST FOR 4TH STRAIGHT TIME, RAISE GDP</u>

Citi's expectations survey: private analysts cut 2026 inflation to 4.02% from 4.09% — the fourth consecutive reduction — and raised growth to 1.2%. Signum Research sees inflation ending the year at 3.07%, inside Banxico's target range. Peso consensus: 17.90 per dollar at year-end.

Reported by El Financiero.

🇲🇽🌾 <u>SUPREME COURT UPHOLDS HOUSING, FOOD AND HEALTHCARE FOR FARMWORKERS</u>

Mexico's SCJN validated the labor reform obliging agribusiness to provide jornaleros dignified housing, food, sanitation and medical care — and denied amparos to three companies that fought it.

Minister President Hugo Aguilar Ortiz recalled San Quintín: workers "lived crammed together, in inhumane conditions... truly lacerating conditions." 3.4 million farmworkers, over 80% informal, now covered.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>THE HIDDEN COST OF PRECARITY: 75% OF MEXICAN WORKERS SUFFER STRESS FATIGUE</u>

Contralínea investigation: 3 in 10 Mexicans will develop a mental disorder and over 60% get no treatment, per IMSS. The Mexican worker logs 2,207 hours a year — nearly 600 more than the OECD average. Anxiety and depression concentrate at ages 20-49: the productive workforce.

Congress just approved cutting the workweek from 48 to 40 hours by 2030, without touching wages. A first step.
